# Gradient, Jacobian, and Hessian

Three objects sit at the heart of every analysis of neural network training: the gradient (which way to step), the Jacobian (sensitivity of vector outputs), and the Hessian (second-order curvature).

## The Gradient as Steepest Ascent Direction

∇f(x) = [∂f/∂x₁, …, ∂f/∂xₙ]ᵀ ∈ ℝⁿ. Normal to level sets, points toward increasing f. The unique vector g satisfying Df(x)[v] = g·v for all v.

## The Jacobian Matrix: Vector-Valued Functions

For f: ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ, J ∈ ℝᵐˣⁿ, Jᵢⱼ = ∂fᵢ/∂xⱼ. Rows = outputs, columns = inputs. Best linear approximation: f(x+v) ≈ f(x) + Jv. The Neural Tangent Kernel K(x,x') = J(x)J(x')ᵀ.

| Object | Shape | Role in ML |
|--------|-------|------------|
| Gradient ∇f | n × 1 | Loss descent direction |
| Jacobian J | m × n | Output/parameter sensitivity, NTK |
| Hessian H | n × n | Curvature, 2nd-order optimizers |

## The Hessian Matrix: Second-Order Curvature

Hᵢⱼ = ∂²f/∂xᵢ∂xⱼ. Taylor: f(x+δ) ≈ f(x) + ∇fᵀδ + ½δᵀHδ. At GPT-4 scale: H has ~1.8×10¹⁴ entries — impossible to materialise.

## Why the Hessian is Symmetric

Schwarz's theorem: ∂²f/∂xᵢ∂xⱼ = ∂²f/∂xⱼ∂xᵢ for C² functions → H = Hᵀ. Real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors, spectral decomposition H = QΛQᵀ.

## Hessian Eigenvalues and Local Curvature

At critical points ∇f(x*)=0: PD (all λᵢ>0) → local min; ND (all λᵢ<0) → local max; indefinite → saddle. Deep network Hessians have bulk eigenvalues near zero with a few large outliers.

## Hessian-Vector Products Without Materialising H

Hv can be computed in O(n) via forward-over-reverse AD: Hv = d/dε[∇f(x+εv)]|_{ε=0}. Cost: 2× backward pass. Enables Hessian-free optimisation, influence functions, eigenvalue estimation.

```python
# HVP with JAX
def hvp(params, v, x, y):
    return jax.jvp(lambda p: jax.grad(loss)(p, x, y), (params,), (v,))[1]
```

## Numerical Computation with Finite Differences

Central difference: f'(x) ≈ [f(x+h)−f(x−h)]/(2h), error O(h²). Optimal h ≈ ε_mach^{1/3} ≈ 10⁻⁵. Use for gradient checking: verify ‖g_analytical − g_numerical‖/(‖g_a‖+‖g_n‖) < 1e-5.
